Auditing historical training-prefix targets measures retrospective, in-sample behavior: success may reflect memorization, and masking the target at inference does not undo its use during fitting. Full-training item counts describe retrospective popularity; time-local counts must include only interactions strictly before each target timestamp, with an explicit window and denominator. Crucially, time-local statistics do not make a model trained on later interactions temporally valid. Temporal generalization requires appropriately time-restricted fitting and unseen future targets; preserve the pinned benchmark and label historical probes separately. [Temporal leakage study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.11060).

For diagnostic comparisons, a defensible design is paired user-cluster bootstrapping: resample users within category, retaining their complete sets of prefixes and paired method results, then recompute the equally weighted four-category macro difference. Use identical negative candidates for both methods on each target and repeat independent candidate draws under the same eligibility rules. Report candidate-draw variability separately from user-bootstrap uncertainty; any combined interval must preserve both dependence structures. These intervals concern fixed trained models, excluding training and search uncertainty. User clustering assumes independent users; shared-item dependence can require additional treatment. Repeated draws reduce Monte Carlo noise but cannot make sampled HR@10 equivalent to full-catalog HR@10. [Dependent-data bootstrap](https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.7406), [sampled-metric limitations](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/).

Treat regime-dependent missingness explicitly: report eligibility, missingness reasons, user counts and target counts by regime; compare methods on common eligible pairs. Undefined probes are missing, not zero. Complete-case contrasts describe that selected population, and bootstrap intervals cannot repair selection bias. Distinguish unavailable diagnostic measurements from unobserved user–item feedback; neither establishes dislike. Propensity corrections require justified observation assumptions and adequate support, not invented exposure probabilities. [Selection-biased recommendation data](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v48/schnabel16.html).
